test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Nov 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

A child learnt the basics of / his mother tongue mainly from / his interactions with the mother.

options.text: A child learnt the basics of

solution:
The correct answer is **"A child learnt the basics of."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in **Part (3)** of the sentence.
 
• The verb "learnt" should be in the present tense form "learns" to correctly reflect an ongoing process.
 
• Hence, **'A child learnt the basics of**' in Part (3) should be replaced with '**A child learns the basics of.**'
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

**Correct sentence:** *A child **learns **the basics of his mother tongue mainly from his interactions with the mother.*​​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In English grammar, the present simple tense (e.g., he learns, they learn) is often used to describe general truths or actions or situations that occur regularly.
 
• **Option 1**: "his mother tongue mainly from," is grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 2**: "No error," is incorrect as there is an error in option 3.
 
• **Option 4**: "his interactions with the mother," is grammatically correct.

1d
